thread:
Prod Pager: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache fragmentation spike on us-west-2 serving pool (svc-ml-infer-#3). latency 95p -> 2.8s, error rate 500s up from 0.2% to 4.6%. Auto-scaling not absorbing due to OOM failures. Paging on-call. Thread root ts: 1803657890

Sarah C.: I'm on it, grabbing logs and allocating pager. first guess: allocator thrash / CUDA fragmentation on hot nodes. Which shards are affected?

Michael L.: seeing it on nodes: i-ml-uw2-14, -18, -22. nvidia-smi shows high used mem but python reports a lot of reserved blocks. Logs: "CUDA malloc failed: out of memory" in torch backend followed by repeated arena growth.

Raj P.: tagging infra to get instance lists and restart plan. @ops-bot can you pull `dmesg` and `journalctl` snippets for those hosts?

ops-bot: Attached: /var/logs/instances/i-ml-uw2-14/dmesg.tail (snippet)
```
[ 1203.412345] device 0: GPU has 12280 MiB total, processes: pids=2
[ 1203.412400] pytorch(2345): CUDA malloc failed at attempt 1 -> OOM
[ 1203.412410] pytorch(2345): cudaMalloc returned error: out of memory
```

Sarah C.: thanks. Running `python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())"` on the pod shows: 
```
|Allocated memory: 11842 MiB
|Reserved memory: 12288 MiB
|Active allocations: 342
|Fragmentation ratio: 0.42
```

Emily T.: also saw continuous batching spike — batch queue depth jumped and some backpressure looped, increasing KV cache growth. Looks like batch config combined with model kv cache growth caused slabs to fragment.

Michael L.: hypothesis: a recent change to batch coalescing allowed larger token windows; combined with a model update that increased KV size, we got large intermittent allocations -> allocator fragmentation -> cudaMalloc OOM.

Sarah C.: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) reduce continuous batch max tokens on route(s) -> stops large coalesced batches 2) set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` on affected workers to reduce fragmentation 3) restart affected pods to reclaim reserved memory. I'll coordinate 1+3 now.

Raj P.: agree. I'm going to patch the route to override batching: `redwoodctl routes patch --service ml-infer --route /v1/generate --set continuous_batching.enabled=false --set continuous_batching.max_tokens=512` (will roll to 2 replicas first). Exec: `redwoodctl routes patch ...`

deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout for route override. Canary on i-ml-uw2-18 and i-ml-uw2-22.

Sarah C.: while rollout is starting, I'm creating a hotfix script to set env vars for pods: `kubectl exec -n ml ns/pod -- env PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` then restart worker process. Will apply to canary first.

Michael L.: note: `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` reduces glibc arenas to limit CPU memory fragmentation; should help host-side fragmentation but test carefully. Also consider `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6,max_split_size_mb:64` — but simpler first.

Sarah C.: applying to canary now. Command run on i-ml-uw2-18 pod: 
```
kubectl -n ml exec pod/ml-worker-18 -- /bin/sh -c '\n  export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64;\n  export MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2;\n  pkill -HUP ml_worker_main || systemctl restart ml-worker\n'
```

ops-bot: Pod ml-worker-18 restarted, pod logs show startup ok.

Michael L.: watching metrics: on canary latency 95p drops from 2.7s -> 860ms, 500s disappear. memory_summary now: 
```
|Allocated memory: 9320 MiB
|Reserved memory: 9728 MiB
|Fragmentation ratio: 0.18
```

Sarah C.: good. rolling to rest of affected nodes now. Rolling restart of rest of pool scheduled, applying env var and restart. ETA ~6 minutes for full roll (staggered 30s intervals).

support-bot: CC @support — initial CS impact list: 12 customers saw degraded responses, 3 reported failures. We're drafting customer messages, ETA to provide updates in 30m.

Raj P.: I'm also applying a short-term batch config global throttle: reduce `batch.max_items` to 8 cluster-wide for the ml-infer pool to reduce burst. Command: `redwoodctl cluster-config set ml-infer.batch.max_items=8 --target us-west-2`

Sarah C.: rollout finished. Post-roll metrics: latency 95p back to 700-900ms, 500s baseline at 0.3%. Errors from allocator OOM gone.

Prod Pager: Incident status changed to: mitigated (hotfix applied, roll completed).

Emily T.: notes for postmortem: root cause likely combo of recent model kv-size increase + batch coalescing change. Allocation pattern created many intermediate large allocations that left small free blocks -> CUDA fragmentation. Suggest immediate follow-ups:
- Create regression test that exercises high token-window coalescing with KV-heavy model.
- Add telemetry for reserved vs allocated memory per GPU to alert before fragmentation hits 30%
- Consider runtime change to proactively compact KV cache when fragmentation crosses threshold
- Review default continuous_batching.max_tokens for high-kv models and add model metadata to prevent aggressive coalescing

Michael L.: I'll open INF ticket and link to this thread: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4387. Assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

Sarah C.: Customer comms: @support, send initial note to affected customers with incident summary and workaround (no action needed from them). I'll prepare a short root-cause blurb after postmortem.

support-bot: Draft message ready, will release after approval.

Raj P.: handing off to overnight oncall (Raj). Handoff note: hotfix env var + route override in place, rollback docs in runbook under /runbooks/kv-frag, watch GPU reserved/allocated ratio and 95p latency for 2h. If fragmentation rises >25% re-run pod restarts + consider temporary capacity scale up.

Sarah C.: thanks all. I'll follow up with postmortem and measurements. Marking thread resolved for now.

Prod Pager: :white_check_mark: RESOLVED: mitigation applied. Incident duration ~7m. Follow-up: INF-4387 (eng-runtime + eng-ml), postmortem due EOD tomorrow.
